subject: Pegasus connector resilience and SLA escalation routine
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Pegasus Partner Success <partners@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Pegasus connector resilience and SLA escalation routine

Hi team,

We're seeing intermittent authentication failures and 503s from the Pegasus connector starting around 2027-05-01 22:00 UTC. Impact: three mid-market customers (account IDs attached in the drive link) experienced degraded inference throughput and retry storms in our gateway. This is visible across three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west).

What we need right now:
- Confirmation that Pegasus has an active incident/triage owning this (we need a priority window within 4 hours).
- Immediate guidance on temporary mitigations (recommended token refresh cadence, rate-limit headers to respect).
- Requested artifacts: a full server-side log bundle and any rate-limiter dashboards. I've attached a short diagnostics snippet from our side for context.

Attachments: redwood_diagnostics_snippets.txt (text) — short excerpts and timestamps.

Please loop in the engineering on-call if you need more telemetry; we can provide pcap/trace windows. If we can't get a timely fix, we need to escalate per the partner SLA so we can coordinate customer communication and potential credits.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

--
On 2027-05-02 at 09:13 Hannah Schmitt wrote above (initial report).

From: Evelyn Moore <evelyn.moore@pegasus.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pegasus Partner Success <partners@pegasus.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus connector resilience and SLA escalation routine

Hannah —

Thanks for the heads up and the diagnostics. We're opening a priority ticket on our side (JIRA-RED-1128) and have routed to our infra triage. To help us accelerate: can you upload the full log bundle to the shared drive link (or reply with the tar) and confirm the exact request IDs / sample timestamps?

Immediate short-term mitigation: please try a token refresh cadence of 45s and enable jittered exponential backoff on your connector (this reduces tight retry loops while we investigate). We'll confirm whether a rate-limiter misconfiguration or token service degradation is the root cause.

I've attached our partner intake form to capture the required artifacts for forensics. If the issue qualifies as an SLA incident (>= 3 affected customers / >30m customer impact), we'll follow the escalation matrix and propose any retro credits as needed.

Attachments: pegasus_request_form.pdf (form) — please complete and return.

Evelyn Moore
Partner Success Lead
Pegasus Systems
evelyn.moore@pegasus.ai
+1 (617) 222-3344

On Tue, May 2, 2027 at 09:13 AM -07:00, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing intermittent authentication failures and 503s from the Pegasus connector starting around 2027-05-01 22:00 UTC...
>

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Pegasus Partner Success <partners@pegasus.ai>, Evelyn Moore <evelyn.moore@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus connector resilience and SLA escalation routine

Evelyn / team —

We reproduced the failure pattern in a staging environment and attached a full log bundle. Key findings from the snippets:
- 2027-05-01T22:07:12Z: repeated 401 responses from token endpoint (pegasus-auth-01) with response_time ~1200ms.
- Shortly after, the connector's retry loop flooded requests and we observed 503s from the downstream inference gateway.
- Client-side token refresh requests spike correlates with the first 401.

Minimal repro steps (staging):
1) Start connector with token TTL set to 60s.
2) Introduce a 1s median delay to token service (simulate load).
3) Observe token refresh collision and subsequent 503s as requests queue behind auth.

Attachments: pegasus_log_bundle.tar.gz (compressed logs, include pegasus-auth-01 traces), redwood_diagnostics_snippets.txt (already provided).

Requests:
- Can you confirm whether the token endpoint has a per-client rate limit that could have been exceeded? If so, what is the per-minute threshold and global burst behaviour?
- ETA for a mitigation from your infra team (patch, config change, or scaling action).

We can deploy a fast client-side mitigator (staggered refresh + lightweight local cache) if you share the recommended refresh header/response format; we'd prefer to avoid a full rollback.

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai

> On May 2, 2027, Evelyn Moore wrote:
>> Thanks for the heads up and the diagnostics...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Moore <evelyn.moore@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus connector resilience and SLA escalation routine

Evelyn —

Thanks for the fast acknowledgement. To keep our customers safe and limit blast radius while your infra team investigates, Redwood proposes the following interim resilience routine (we can iterate):

1) Client-side mitigations (we will roll):
   - Implement jittered exponential backoff for token refresh with a maximum of 6 retries.
   - Add a 250–750ms randomized token refresh delay to spread refresh windows across pods.
   - Maintain a local token cache per process for up to 90s to absorb transient auth slowness.

2) Partner actions (Pegasus):
   - Confirm token endpoint per-client rate limits and provide recommended refresh headers by EOD 2027-05-04.
   - Share any short-term scaling plan or config changes you will apply (ETA).

3) Canary & SLA coordination:
   - Schedule a canary patch for 2027-05-06T02:00:00Z (low-traffic window) to validate the fix.
   - If the fix does not materially reduce errors, Redwood will request compensation per section 4.2 of the partner SLA. To expedite, please sign the emergency amendment I linked below (DocuSign).

DocuSign: https://docu.sign/example/amendment-3492
Jira ticket: JIRA-RED-1128 (please set priority: P0)

If we don't see a firm mitigation ETA within 24 hours, we'll escalate to our Partnerships Director to secure an executive path. We appreciate your partnership on this — customers are impacted and transparency will help us all.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Success Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (212) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: pegasus_request_form.pdf (previous), pegasus_log_bundle.tar.gz (uploaded to shared drive).
